beats.title: The landing page (trimmed) - thesis, competitors, architecture, receipt
beats.narration: I'm Abhishek. This is Whodunit, built for the Agents of SigNoz hackathon - Track 2, Signals and Dashboards. When production breaks, every observability tool shows you the difference between the traces that failed and the ones that didn't. BubbleUp, Trace Patterns, Grafana's compare - they rank attributes and hand you a panel. Then a human re-types that finding into a query, at three in the morning. Whodunit closes that loop. One ClickHouse scan, mine the pattern that separates the cohorts, compile it into a real SigNoz query, verify it against the live engine, and arm it as an alert. Five stages, and no LLM anywhere.
beats.notes: b9.mp4 re-trimmed to [1.0, 45.6] as docs/video/raw/b9t.mp4 (44.60s); b9.mp4 itself is untouched. 1.0s comes off the head (the hero sits static until the scroll starts at ~3.2s) and 0.5s off the tail (the proof hold runs from ~44s, so a full second of it survives). It opens the film now, so the whole crawl is kept: hero (13.1x / 61 = 61 / 6 of 6 / 0 LLM chips and the honest banner) -> the 'nobody hands you the query' competitor table -> the five deterministic stages -> the five SigNoz surfaces -> the hold on the compiled (A => B) && NOT C, the verdict hash, the 6/6 table and the cache_bypass loss-then-fix note.

beats.title: The citation - SigNoz/signoz#1957, still open
beats.narration: And this isn't a problem I invented for a hackathon. SigNoz's co-founder asked for exactly this, three and a half years ago - still open.
beats.notes: Title, #1957, Open badge, pranay01, Jan 2 2023 all legible before the scroll. Recorded headless with Playwright.

beats.title: Sketch - the fault, drawn (why neither condition alone works)
beats.narration: Here's the fault, drawn. A healthy checkout calls the flag service. A failing one retries redis, and the flag-service span is missing. But the retry alone shows up in healthy traces too. And plenty of healthy traces skip the flag check. Neither condition alone separates them - only both at once.
beats.notes: Rendered, not recorded: tools/video/sketch/render_s1.py draws 711 matplotlib plt.xkcd() frames at 1920x1080 and ffmpeg encodes them at 30fps. Same palette/ink as docs/assets/flow-pipeline.png. Progressive reveal: healthy trace tree -> failing trace tree (amber redis-retry edge, dashed ghost flag-service with an X) -> the retry circled on BOTH sides -> the missing flag circled on BOTH sides -> a green box around both conditions on the failing side only, with the seed-778 numbers 13.1x lift, 61 bad / 0 healthy.

beats.title: One scan, THE ELIMINATION BOARD
beats.narration: One question to ClickHouse. Then the whole lattice is enumerated locally. The machine weighs the obvious answers - the edge alone - and rejects them. Only the conjunction separates the cohorts, at thirteen times lift.
beats.notes: One real 472.3s run; the spinner plays that wait back in 5s with its counter ramping to the true elapsed, which is then printed.

beats.title: The flat baseline fails on the same cohort
beats.narration: This is what every flat tool sees - BubbleUp, compare, Trace Patterns. Its best single predicate lands at precision zero point one seven. The fault needs two conditions at once.
beats.notes: benchmark/baseline.py on the identical matrix. Top pick NOT edge__shop_checkout__GET_flags_evaluate, precision 0.17, recall 1.00 - fails the 0.80/0.50 gate.

beats.title: Compiled query + verification receipt
beats.narration: No model wrote this. It's compiled into SigNoz's own grammar - A implies B, and not C - then run back against the engine. Mined sixty-one. SigNoz returned sixty-one.
beats.notes: Leaves A/B/C, (A => B) && NOT C, returnSpansFrom A, then the differential receipt and the verdict hash.

beats.title: Sketch - one store, not three (why it has to be SigNoz)
beats.narration: And this is why it has to be SigNoz. Traces and logs live in one ClickHouse, so a single scan joins them by trace ID. On Tempo plus Loki, that join doesn't exist.
beats.notes: Rendered the same way (tools/video/sketch/render_s2.py, 462 frames). Three disconnected drums - Tempo/traces, Loki/logs, Prometheus/metrics - with the arrows between them struck out in red and captioned 'no join'; then one SigNoz - ClickHouse drum holding traces + logs + metrics with a JOIN ON trace_id arrow and 'one scan'. Closing line: one clickhouse_sql scan joins traces JOIN logs, impossible on three stores. on_screen is empty on purpose - the sketch quotes no run-specific counters.

beats.title: The permalink, opened in SigNoz Trace Explorer
beats.narration: That permalink opens the machine-written query in SigNoz's own Trace Explorer - all three leaves and the operator, rendered in the real UI. The result set collapses to the matched traces. Open one, and the flame graph shows the shape: payment retries redis, and flag-service never ran.
beats.notes: compositeQuery is double-URL-encoded and carries builder.queryTraceOperator (materialize/NOTES.md 1). The Explorer renders all three leaves and the operator, and the flame graph shows redis-retry under shop-payment with no shop-flag-service span. Tail trimmed: the flame graph held static ~6s past the narration.

beats.title: Arm it - and it fires
beats.narration: One flag arms it. The discriminator becomes a native v2alpha1 alert with warning and critical thresholds. Replay the fault, and at t plus one eighty-two seconds the webhook fires - the rule ID in that payload is the rule the command just created. Everyone else in this category stops at a panel.
beats.notes: Armed live (rule 019f97fb-f4a7-743a-8499-be519fb5bbeb); the middle segment is SigNoz's own Alert Rules page showing the rule plotted against both threshold lines. The ~1-3 min evaluation delay is cut out of one continuous take.

beats.title: Abstention - and the one it first got wrong
beats.narration: Here's what matters more. Point it at a decoy - an attribute that tracks failure but doesn't cause it - and it abstains. Point it at a healthy system, it abstains again. Across six seeded faults, it never named a false culprit. And this one it first got wrong - it abstained where a real answer existed. I found the seam, fixed it, and left the original failure in the repo.
beats.notes: Termcast, same offscreen pipeline as b2/b3/b4. tools/video/demo_abstention.py renders benchmark/results.json - the record of the 946.5s live benchmark run behind REPORT.md. Board: 6/6 pass, 0 false culprits, ABSTAIN on decoys + null_scenario, PARTIAL on retry_storm. Then cache_bypass: the original ABSTAIN, the absence-only compiler refusal quoted from the run, the MDL dominance prune, the _select_finding fix, and the re-run - (A => B) && NOT (C => D), recall 1.0, precision 1.0, 160/160 live match, original failure kept in benchmark/ISSUES.md #2. on_screen is empty on purpose: these numbers come from the benchmark, not from the seed-778 explain-result.json that real_numbers reads.

beats.title: Determinism - two live runs, one hash
beats.narration: Run it twice. Same input, same seed, same verdict hash. There is no LLM anywhere in the runtime - this is deterministic. The corpus is synthetic and disclosed; ground truth comes from a manifest.
beats.notes: Two complete live runs (scan, mine the whole lattice, compile, verify). The mining waits are played back compressed; the hashes are not touched. Spinner wait for run 2 (16-21s) spliced out; both hashes still land.

beats.title: The replay app - step through the run in a browser
beats.narration: And you don't need my machine to check any of it. The whole run is stepped through in the browser - the board, the compiled query, the receipt, the hash - hosted, no install.
beats.notes: replay/app.html at 1920x1080, served locally on :8099 and byte-identical to the deployed Space. Lands on the shell, then ArrowRight x3 to the elimination board, the compiled trace-operator and the verification receipt, where 'Run differential verification' snaps in mined 61 / SigNoz 61 / MATCH. The viewport never moves: document height equals viewport height and only #panel scrolls. Keyboard-only, so no cursor is in frame.

beats.title: The repo and the one command that reproduces it
beats.narration: Everyone can show you the difference. Only SigNoz can arm it. Everything's on GitHub - one command reproduces the whole run, casting file and lock committed.
beats.notes: foundryctl cast is typed but deliberately not run - the live stack already owns :8080 / :4318. casting.yaml.lock is committed next to it.
